sections.heading: Reworked BlastGang mode
sections.text:
BlastGang has received a major overhaul of its core mechanics:
- An in-match economy has been introduced.
- The Device activation system has been reworked. The Device now explodes when its activation timer reaches zero.
- Presets have been replaced with an in-match gear shop.

When we created BlastGang, we thought weapon customization alone would provide the mode with enough depth and variety. Over time, it became clear that we'd underestimated one of its most important components: the in-match economy.

With this rework, we decided to return to the mode's roots and take another look at how players make decisions throughout a match: when to save, when to take risks, and what to spend their hard-earned resources on.

sections.heading: Gear shop
sections.text:
Players no longer need to select a preset before the match. Everyone starts on equal footing and purchases weapons, armor, and helmets at the beginning of each round using money earned during the match.

Grenades have also been moved to the shop, with purchase limits applying to both the team and individual players.

At the same time, we've preserved the deep customization players are used to: the shop's inventory can be changed, and weapons can be customized to suit your playstyle.

sections.heading: Device
sections.text:
The Device, the mode's key element, has also undergone major changes. The Device now explodes when its timer expires: no player can survive within the blast radius, and the shockwave deals damage across a significant portion of the map.

Device activation is now split into two three-second stages. Both stages can still be completed in a single interaction, but if activation is canceled after the first three seconds, the first stage is counted as completed, and only the second stage needs to be completed.

sections.heading: Armory
sections.text:
The approach to calculating Meta Score has been changed: weapon modifications can now account for up to 40% of the preset's total cost.
- Weapon modification costs were significantly increased.
- Weapon, ammunition, and magazine costs were reduced.
- Meta Score for plate carriers, helmets, and additional mods were reworked: protection zones and penalties now have a greater impact on the final score.
- Base medical item costs were reduced.

These balance changes are designed around the idea that a weapon's build and stats will determine how many magazines, protective items, and medical supplies a player can bring in their preset.

We hope to create a system where players have to balance firepower, protection, and medical supplies, making it impossible to build the best weapon without giving up some of their gear or medical supplies.

sections.heading: Armor rebalance
sections.text:
Recently, we’ve seen increasing feedback that TTK (time-to-kill) has become too quick. In combat, players often don’t get a second chance, and prolonged firefights have become less common. This also negatively impacts match pacing and spectacle.

To slightly slow down TTK, we decided to grant +1 armor class to the most vulnerable classes.
- Assault will now be able to absorb more damage, while Scout receives a specially configured Class 6 plate with unique characteristics.
- Scout will retain only Class 3 protection masks and gain more chest protection at the cost of head protection, while Enforcer remains the most heavily armored class.

We hope these changes will increase the number of exciting duel-like firefights where player aiming skill plays the key role in securing victory.
- The cost of all ballistic plates in the game has been proportionally reduced to preserve comfortable preset building options.

sections.heading: Assault
sections.text:
- Armor: 4 → 5 ceramic;
- Helmet: 4 with ear protection → 4 with no ear protection but with armor attachments, excluding ULACH.

sections.heading: Scout
sections.text:
- Armor: 5 ceramic → 6 special plate;
- Helmet: 4 with no ear protection but with armor attachments → 3 masks.

sections.heading: Marksman
sections.text: - Helmet: 4 with no ear protection but with armor attachments → 4 with ear protection.

sections.heading: АSh-12 and RPDN
sections.text:
We are aware of the ongoing discussions surrounding the effectiveness of the ASh-12 assault rifle and the RPDN machine gun. At the moment, these are among the most popular weapons and generate frustration among players who do not use them. At first glance, they appear to require nerfs. However, with the increased armor levels across classes, we believe their effectiveness will naturally decrease and become more aligned with other weapons.

That said, we are applying a small nerf to the PS12B cartridge so that it penetrates Class 5 armor slightly less consistently.
- Reduced the PS12B ammo penetration from 46 to 45;
- Significantly reduced the armor damage.
We will continue monitoring statistics and player feedback and make additional adjustments if necessary.

sections.heading: Laser device cost increase
sections.text:
Tactical devices do more than simply help with aiming. Functionally, they also reduce hip-fire spread. Hip-fire tactics at medium and long ranges with sniper rifles and machine guns have become increasingly common. We want to reward deliberate aimed fire more strongly and make tactical devices a meaningful investment rather than a cheap preset filler.
- Increased the Meta Score for all laser devices by 100-230.

sections.heading: Laser device availability
sections.text:
Enforcer remained the only class untouched by the rebalance, so after the changes it may lack the penetration needed to perform confidently against opponents. To strengthen suppressive fire, we are allowing tactical devices to be used on all weapons available to the class, especially since players were already mounting them on machine guns by transferring them from pistols.
- Enforcer can now equip laser devices on all available weapons.

sections.heading: Medicine cost decrease
sections.text:
Medkits in Arena are often difficult to use in time during combat. We want to slightly reduce the cost of medical setups to give players more flexibility when building presets.
- All available medkits, bandages, tourniquets, and splints are now cheaper by 5-50 Meta Score.

sections.heading: SPP ammo
sections.text:
Due to changes introduced in Patch 0.5.0, 9x39 weapons using SPP ammunition lost some of their relevance. Providing the Scout SR-3M or AS VAL Mod.4 with PAB-9 would be too risky, so we decided to slightly increase SPP armor penetration to make these weapons more comfortable to use.
- Increased the 9x39 SPP ammo penetration from 35 to 37.

sections.heading: VSK-94 and 9A-91
AK and MAI AP
sections.text:
7.62x39 AKs have always occupied a very narrow niche and were rarely used by players. While their recoil was significantly improved in Patch 0.5.0, we want to give players an additional tool to reconsider these weapons.
- AKMN, AKMSN, AK-103, and AK-104 assault rifles now have access to MAI AP ammunition.

sections.heading: MCX-SPEAR 25-round magazines
sections.text:
MCX-SPEAR was heavily affected by the Patch 0.5.0 rebalance. It had long remained at the top of the meta and was surrounded by constant debate, so a nerf was expected.

However, after removing the 25-round magazines, we noticed players were unwilling to experiment with the weapon again, causing many of its stat adjustments to go unnoticed. In addition, related weapons such as the MDR 7.62x51 also suffered indirectly.

We are bringing back the 25-round magazines for the MCX-SPEAR to restore some of its popularity, but keep in mind: this is no longer the same SPEAR as before.
- Added back 25-round magazines for the MCX-SPEAR, available for 30 GP at progression level 4 for and only for the Assault class.

sections.heading: Heavy bolt-action ergonomics increase
sections.text:
After improvements to 7.62x51 and 7.62x54R bolt-action ammunition, large-caliber rifles became less relevant because their ammunition effectiveness became nearly identical, while the cost, weight, and ergonomics of the AXMC and SAKO M10 remained problematic.

We are slightly improving the ergonomics of these weapons to make them more comfortable to use.
- AI AXMC – increased the ergonomics by 8;
- Sako TRG M10 – increased the ergonomics by 5.

In this update, we aim to increase the value of unlocking individual weapon mods:

We also want to eliminate the situation where most Armory items could be unlocked by playing a single weapon. The following changes have been introduced:
- Duplicate mods have been completely removed from weapon progression trees.
- To unlock a specific modification, players must now reach the required progression level on the corresponding weapon.

sections.heading: Meta score rebalance
sections.text:
With Patch 0.5.0, we are introducing experimental changes to the Meta score limits. Previously, the limits of each of the four bars had to be considered when assembling a valid preset, helping maintain balance and variety in EFT: Arena. At the same time, the system felt overloaded, especially for new players.

We are temporarily removing restrictions for three Meta score bars: Firepower, Defense, and Utility. This will give players complete freedom in building presets, but may result in unbalanced “meme” builds appearing in matches.

We are closely monitoring this experiment and will decide on the future of the Meta score system based on your feedback. Your opinion matters — feel free to share it on our social media!

sections.heading: Balancing changes
sections.text: As part of Patch 0.3, we were tasked with reducing the total number of headshot kills, which at the time had statistically reached over 70%. Although headshots are natural for competitive shooters, we wanted to find an average value at which the equipment of the classes also gave the player the opportunity to react to the enemy. The value of headshots we saw after the balancing adjustments unfortunately turned out to be much lower than we expected.

sections.heading: Enforcer adjustments
sections.text:
With previous updates we made several adjustments to the Enforcer class to give more variety and playability to shotguns to make the class more heavy weapons related, but we didn't take into account a number of balancing factors for this class which led to situations where shooting at the legs became much more advantageous and easier.

We've put together a comprehensive list of changes for the class aimed at correcting this situation and bringing back a healthier balance between classes. As a result of the changes, the concept of the Enforcer will shift towards a more flexible one that is able to take advantage of the variation of available weapons while remaining effective in both defense and offense, still having weaknesses.

- Reduced the limb damage (Arms and Legs) from 1 to 0.8;
- Reduced the destroyed limb damage (Arms) from 1 to 0.8.

sections.heading: Enforcer balancing changes
Scout adjustments
sections.text: Within our class concept, the Scout was supposed to be a powerful class, as it has access to the most effective ammo and a wide list of weapons. After the Patch 0.3, Scout retained its role, but having class 4 armor made it too versatile, which made it more competitive with the Assault class. As part of the current changes, we want to weaken its access to armor, but keep access to ammo and weapons.

sections.heading: Iceberg location
sections.text:
Added a new location for BlastGang and CheckPoint modes.

A hotel rebuilt from an old Soviet resort for elites and their families. Located in a scenic area right on the bank of a bend of an unnamed river. All around is pure nature. So much so that access to the hotel is available only by a single road or a cable car. The residents appreciated the place for its seclusion and the opportunity to be at one with nature. On the territory of the hotel is a cable car leading to a smoother river bank area.

The hotel was constructed in the 2000s with funding from a few anonymous investors. Local activists staged pickets against the river bank development, proposing options where the old Soviet hotel is turned into part of an eco-trail. However, their proposals were rejected. Rumor has it that local mayor Vishnevsky had a hand in the building permit.

The residents included many famous personalities and representatives of the government office. High-ranking TerraGroup employees often visited the hotel. Several meeting rooms were specially remodeled for them and closed off from the rest of the residents.

After the tragic events in Tarkov, the hotel was closed for reconstruction. At least that's what the dry announcement on the official website said. In reality, the place was still visited several times by representatives of TerraGroup, and after that the territory was taken over by the future founders of the Arena and redesigned for gladiator fights.

sections.heading: Player profile
Custom preset system
sections.text:
Added the ability to create a fully custom preset. You can customize the equipment available for each class, weapons and attachments, contents of chest rigs/plate carriers and pockets, and the character appearance through different uppers/lowers and masks/hats/eyeglasses.

A total of 12 custom preset slots will be available to players, 3 for each class.

Custom preset rules:
- Each piece of equipment has its own metascore value, a universal unit for evaluating the item effectiveness;
- You can use and customize any equipment available to the class;
- Custom presets have 4 metascore bars: Firepower, Defense, Utility, and Total metascore value:
  - Firepower bar displays the meta score for your weapon, ammo, and weapon mods;
  - Defense bar displays the meta score for all armor elements and items with protective properties;
  - Utility bar displays the meta score for medicine, gear rigs, and headsets;
  - Metascore bar displays total potential preset power.
- Each bar has lower and upper limits. When creating a preset, you need to balance its equipment in such a way that the amount of metascore does not exceed the bar limits.

Starter presets
- Reworked the standard presets for all classes: there are now three starter presets available in each class. All equipment from the standard presets is available immediately and can be used to create your own preset.

Collectible presets
- Collectible presets will be improved and adapted for the custom preset system and returned to the game in the nearest updates.

Tiers
- The preset Tier system has been fully removed from the game.

Class system
- The CQB class has been renamed to Enforcer.
- Each piece of equipment is assigned to a class. The equipment can be available for all classes or only for specific classes.

sections.heading: Armory
sections.text:
Added Armory to the game. The Armory acts as an equipment store and handbook.

You can buy equipment for two main currencies: Roubles and GP Coins

- To purchase some equipment, you will also need to meet certain conditions, such as: completing daily tasks or reaching a certain character level;
- Some equipment will become available when you unlock or purchase certain weapons, such as basic weapon attachments for this weapon;
- Some equipment is available immediately at the start of the game.

In the Armory, you can see the links for any equipment. For example, you can see what equipment can be installed on a particular item.

All ammo and armor elements (ballistic plates), except for a few ballistic plates, are available immediately and do not require purchasing and unlocking.

The cost and conditions for unlocking new items have been balanced. Thus, every player, regardless of the result in the match, will be able to purchase the items they want. We will continue to closely monitor the progression balance and make adjustments if necessary.

sections.heading: New game mode - BlastGang
sections.text:
- BlastGang is a 5v5 team battle with asymmetrical gameplay. The attacking side needs to plant a special device, and the defending side needs to prevent or deactivate the planted device.
- The game mode is available in both Ranked and Unranked modes.
- The mode can be played on Bay 5, Bowl, and SkyBridge.

sections.heading: SkyBridge
sections.text:
- A new location, SkyBridge, has been added to the game.
- A railway station which connected Tarkov with the rest of the cities of Norvinsk region. It was opened after reconstruction just before the conflict. Now used as a death arena.
- In this update, the location is available for LastHero and BlastGang game modes. In future updates, the location will also be available for TeamFight mode.

sections.heading: New game mode - Last Hero
sections.text:
- The Last Hero mode is now available for the unranked game mode.
- Last Hero is a deathmatch between several players. The goal of each player is to get the most kills in the allotted time.
- At the beginning of the match and after each death, players will be able to change the equipment preset and instantly return to the battle.
- After 10 minutes, the match ends. Players are ranked based on the number of kills they have accumulated.
- The player's reward depends on the place taken in the match:
  - The experience in the reward for unlocking presets is distributed as follows:
    - Experience for kills is credited to the preset on which the kill was made
    - Looting, healing and rank place experience is divided between classes, depending on the effectiveness of those classes in the match. The effectiveness of a class is affected by the number of kills and damage dealt on that class' presets
    - There is only one double experience bonus per match for a particular class. The choice of class for the bonus depends on which class gained the most experience during the match.
- Before the start, players can select the Tier on which the match will be played;
- All presets within the selected Tier are free and available for selection, regardless of the number of presets a player has unlocked.

- Increased the change of ARP reward and loss after a match depending on the difference between the player's ARP and the average ARP of the opponent's team
  - The greater the difference, the more the player with a lower average ARP will receive in case of victory and the less will lose in case of defeat, and vice versa - the greater the difference, the less the player with a higher average ARP will receive in case of victory and the more will lose in case of defeat.

  - First 2 presets of each class are free by default

  - Significantly reduced the number of frag grenades in all presets

- Unlocking matchmaking in the next preset Tier requires unlocking 5 presets of the next Tier
- Matchmaking now accounts for player ARP and the selected preset Tier
- Preset Tiers 2 and 3 will be temporarily locked from matchmaking in ranked games until there are enough players who have unlocked Tiers 2 and 3 respectively

sections.heading: New hitbox and armor system from EFT versions 0.14.0.0 and 0.14.1.0
Hitboxes
sections.text:
- The head is divided into separate simple hit zones that coincide with the protection zones of helmets and masks
- Three hit zones have been added to the head area: Throat, Neck, and Face colliders
- Thorax and stomach hit zones are divided into front, back and sides
- Pelvic hit zone is divided into Groin and Buttocks. Hitting these areas inflicts damage to the Stomach area

sections.heading: Armor
sections.text:
- Protection of armor and helmets is divided into separate zones, depending on which section this zone covers (in some cases it might be several zones). These are the slots with integrated armor. Integrated armor zones have their own separate durability. For example, you can now reduce your opponent's chest zone armor durability and not damage the durability of other armor zones if you shoot them in the chest. Integrated armor usually has armor class 2 or 3
- An armored collar that protects the neck hitbox has been added for a large number of body armor pieces
- In addition, ballistic plate slots and integrated armor slots have been added to body armor vests and plate carriers: for chest section, for back section, and for side sections. Ballistic plates usually have armor class 3-6
- The dimensions of the ballistic plate zones are the same as the average dimensions of real ballistic plates of that format
- Body armor protection is no longer uniform. It now depends on what areas the body armor visually protects. For example, no body armor protects the armpit area

sections.heading: Damage and armor
sections.text:
- Reworked the damage through layers of armor: now when each layer is penetrated, the bullet loses some penetration power and damage depending on the characteristics of the penetrated armor
- Blunt damage now decreases when there is soft armor behind the unpenetrated component
- Removed the possibility for bullets to pierce through a character's thorax and stomach
